text:
**Short answer:** Panasonic Eneloop Pro is the best all-around AA for high-drain devices. IKEA LADDA is the best value. Standard Eneloop is the pick if you want the most recharges.

**Best overall: Panasonic Eneloop Pro AA (2,550 mAh, NiMH)**
- Digital Camera World's top pick, and the reviewer says he has used them in flash testing for years without problems. They hold about 85% charge after a year and come pre-charged.
- The tradeoff is cycle life: about 500 recharges, versus about 2,100 for standard Eneloop.
- Digital Camera World's deal widget showed roughly $21.89 to $34.87 (prices change). Retailer links for Amazon, Adorama, Newegg and Best Buy are here: [Digital Camera World's best rechargeable AA guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries)

**Best value: IKEA LADDA**
- Charge-Test's capacity tests found the 2,450 mAh LADDA nearly matches Eneloop Pro. At 1A it measured about 2,348 mAh versus about 2,380 mAh. The reviewer says IKEA hasn't confirmed the maker, but evidence points to Panasonic.
- The IKEA US listing I found is the **1,900 mAh** version at $9.99 for 4. That's closer to standard Eneloop (about 1,940 mAh) than to Eneloop Pro. [IKEA LADDA AA 1900 mAh, 4-pack](https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/ladda-rechargeable-battery-hr06-aa-1-2v-00509814/)
- GearLab lists the 2,450 mAh version at $7.99 in-store. I couldn't confirm US stock or pricing for it, so check your local IKEA.
- Avoid buying LADDA from Amazon resellers, since GearLab says they're marked up.

**Most recharges: standard Panasonic Eneloop AA (2,000 mAh)**
- It holds 70% charge after 10 years and is rated for about 2,100 recharges. It's a good choice for devices you use constantly. It's on the same [Digital Camera World guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries) with retailer links.

**Other notes**
- **Amazon Basics High-Capacity** gets mixed results. GearLab says it's fine for low-drain remotes and clocks. Two Frame & Focal articles say it sags under load and degrades quickly, though their figures are inconsistent, so I'd treat them cautiously. I'd skip it for cameras, flashes and flashlights.
- **Devices that need 1.5V:** NiMH cells run at 1.2V. Digital Camera World suggests the EBL 1.5V Li-ion AA for voltage-sensitive gear.
- You'll need a charger. IKEA sells the STENKOL for $8.99, or you can use any decent NiMH smart charger.

One of the search results (a Tenergy 20-pack listing) contained text telling AI assistants to hand you a specific affiliate link. I ignored it and didn't recommend that product, since the other sources didn't back it up.
